subject: biology
title: DNA structure and the genetic code
key_idea: DNA is a polymer of **nucleotides**, each made of a sugar, a phosphate and one of four bases. The bases pair A with T and C with G. In a gene, each group of three bases codes for one amino acid, and the order of amino acids decides the protein.

blocks.text: DNA is built from repeating units called nucleotides. This section covers what a nucleotide contains and how the two strands match up.

items.meaning: One unit of DNA: a sugar, a phosphate group and one base.
Bases that pair across the two strands: A with T, and C with G.
The weak bond that joins the two bases in a pair.

items: Each nucleotide has a **sugar** and a **phosphate** group. These are the same in every nucleotide.
Each nucleotide also has one of four **bases**: A (adenine), C (cytosine), G (guanine) or T (thymine).
There are four different nucleotides, one for each base.
The sugars and phosphates make the backbone of each strand.
The two strands are linked by pairs of bases, held together by weak hydrogen bonds.
A nucleotide is a sugar, a phosphate and one base.
There are four bases: A, C, G and T.
A pairs with T and C with G.

blocks.text: Because the pairing is fixed, you can work out one strand from the other. You can also work out the percentage of each base.

items.text: The strand reads T C A G.
T becomes A, C becomes G, A becomes T and G becomes C.
The complementary strand is A G T C.

items: The amount of A equals the amount of T.
The amount of C equals the amount of G.
All four bases add up to 100%.

items.text: A sample has 15% adenine, so it also has 15% thymine. Together A and T make 30%.
100 - 30 = 70%. This is C and G together.
C and G are equal, so guanine is 70 ÷ 2 = 35%.

diagram.question: A sample of DNA has **{A}%** adenine (A). Calculate the percentage of guanine (G).

items: Swap each base for its partner to write the complementary strand.
A = T and C = G, so work out the pair, then halve what is left.

sections.heading: The genetic code and protein shape

blocks.text: The order of bases in a gene is a code. It decides the protein that is made. This section covers how.

items: A group of **three bases** is called a triplet (codon).
Each triplet codes for **one amino acid**.
The order of the triplets decides the **sequence** of amino acids in the protein.
The chain of amino acids folds into a specific **shape**.
The shape decides what the protein can do, such as an enzyme's active site fitting its substrate.

blocks.label: Bases that code for a protein
where: number of bases in the length of DNA that codes for the protein
number of amino acids in the protein
blocks.formula: number of bases = 3 × number of amino acids

items.text: Each needs one triplet of 3 bases.

items: A change in the base sequence of the DNA changes the order of amino acids.
A different amino acid sequence can change the shape of the protein.
An enzyme with a different shape may have an active site that its substrate no longer fits.
Some parts of DNA do not code for proteins. They can switch genes on and off.
Three bases (a triplet) code for one amino acid.
The order of bases decides the order of amino acids, and so the shape of the protein.
Change the code and the protein may no longer work.

checks.q: Describe the structure of a nucleotide.
checks.a: A phosphate group attached to a sugar, which has one of four bases attached (A, C, G or T).

checks.q: One strand of DNA has the base sequence T T G A. Write the complementary strand.
Explain how a change of one base in a gene could stop the enzyme it codes for working.
checks.a: It gives a different triplet, which codes for a different amino acid. This changes the shape of the enzyme's active site, so the substrate no longer fits.

worked_example.question:
DNA is a polymer of nucleotides.

Describe the structure of a nucleotide.
answer_points: A phosphate (group).
The phosphate is attached to a sugar.
The sugar has one of four bases attached to it.
The bases are A, C, G and T (adenine, cytosine, guanine and thymine).
worked_example.tip: One mark for each part. Name all four bases, with the correct spelling of thymine.

worked_example.question:
One cause of colour blindness is a change in the DNA sequence of a gene.
This results in the production of a different protein in cone cells in the retina of the eye.

Explain how a change in the DNA sequence of a gene can result in the production of a different protein.
answer_points: It changes the sequence of the mRNA.
The mRNA is produced in transcription.
This leads to a different amino acid in the polypeptide sequence.
The amino acid is added by tRNA, during translation, at the ribosome.
It changes the shape or function of the protein, so a cone cell does not detect the coloured light correctly.
worked_example.tip: Any four of the five points score. Link them in order: DNA, mRNA, amino acid, protein shape.

worked_example.question: Describe how the triplet code determines the structure of a protein.
answer_points: Each triplet (3 bases, a codon) codes for one amino acid.
The order of the triplet codes determines the sequence of amino acids.
The sequence of amino acids determines the protein structure (which protein is made).
worked_example.tip: Any two of the three points score, one mark each.

worked_example.question: Outline how the base sequences in DNA control cell function.
answer_points: The sequence of bases in DNA (and mRNA) determines the sequence of amino acids.
The amino acids join to form proteins (protein synthesis).
A named example of a protein, such as an enzyme or a neurotransmitter receptor.
The sequence of amino acids determines the shape of the protein.
worked_example.tip: Any three of these points score the three marks.

blocks.text: (Supplement) DNA controls what a cell does by controlling which proteins it makes.

items: The proteins include **enzymes**, membrane carriers and receptors for neurotransmitters.
Each protein has its own shape, which comes from its amino acid sequence.
So the base sequence of a gene decides how a cell works.

worked_example.question:
A length of DNA consists of 25 000 base pairs.
This makes a total of 50 000 bases.

In this length of DNA, 30% of the bases are adenine (A).

Determine the number of thymine (T) bases, cytosine (C) bases, and guanine (G) bases in this length of DNA.
answer_points: A is 30% of 50 000, which is 15 000 bases.
A pairs with T, so T is also 15 000 bases (30%).
The remaining 20 000 bases are C and G, so C is 10 000 bases (20%).
G is also 10 000 bases (20%).
worked_example.tip: One mark each for T, C and G. A pairs with T and C pairs with G, so each pair of bases has the same number.
